claim: The TCI per-probe status in state/HOST_SNAPSHOT.evidence.json is a coarse aggregate over a multi-command shell line and contradicts its own stdout in at least 7 probes (storage.dev_ls, storage.mdadm_conf, bmc.ipmi_dev_perms, network.firewall_active, storage.smartctl_scan, network.sshd_test_config, services.watchdog); network.sshd_test_config and network.sshd_g_effective record the exit code of head, not sshd (rc=0 / rc=141 SIGPIPE).
design_impact: Derive facts from per-line evidence, never from probe status. The sensor records outcome per individual observation (exit status, errno, stderr) and never reads an exit code through a shell pipeline.

claim: /etc/mdadm/mdadm.conf EXISTS on the host (18 bytes, content HOMEHOST <ignore>); only /etc/mdadm.conf is ENOENT. The earlier snapshot prose listing mdadm.conf as absent was wrong and has been corrected in state/HOST_SUMMARY.md and tooling/build_snapshot.py.
design_impact: A RAID check must test both paths and must not read a stock HOMEHOST-only file as evidence of configured arrays. Snapshot-prose claim RETRACTED (F90).

claim: Linux v6.8 drivers/firmware/dmi-id.c hardcodes mode 0400 on product_serial, product_uuid, board_serial, chassis_serial and 0444 on every other DMI attribute (vendor, product, board, chassis, bios, asset tags). Host-confirmed by ls -l of /sys/class/dmi/id (18 attributes 0444, 4 attributes 0400 root). The split has been contested upstream, so it is kernel-version dependent, not a guarantee.
design_impact: Attempt every read and classify by errno; serials/UUID are UNKNOWN+EACCES unprivileged (correct behaviour, not a defect); asset tags and vendor/model ARE readable and must be read (under-claiming them is a bug).

claim: Every raw SMBIOS route is root-only: /sys/firmware/dmi/tables/{DMI,smbios_entry_point} and ALL attributes under /sys/firmware/dmi/entries/<type>-<inst>/ (handle, instance, length, position, raw, type) are 0400 with a CAP_SYS_ADMIN gate; /sys/firmware/efi/systab is 0400; /dev/mem is root:kmem. Only the entry DIRECTORY names (0755, listable) are usable unprivileged. Host-confirmed (R4-OR7): entries 38-0 and 42-0 listable, every attribute EACCES.
design_impact: readdir of /sys/firmware/dmi/entries is an unprivileged presence oracle (type 38 = IPMI device, type 42 = Redfish host interface); every field-level SMBIOS claim is UNKNOWN+EACCES. Kills u-root/pkg/smbios, go-smbios, dmidecode as options. R4-F30 phrasing (raw only) superseded by R4-F49.

claim: Owner/tenant is not determinable on this host: /etc/machine-info and /etc/motd are ENOENT, DMI asset/version/family fields are vendor placeholders (To be filled by O.E.M., Chassis Asset Tag, 0123456789, Family), and the world-readable cloud-init instance-data.json has empty hostname/plan/tags with merged_cfg literally redacted for non-root user. Provider (Latitude.sh) and facility (CHI) are the only readable hints.
design_impact: owner = explicit unknown + owner_candidates (provider datasource class, facility, sshd drop-in provenance) + the readable asset tags; placeholder detection is a generic pattern class, never a literal match.

claim: machine-id(5) declares /etc/machine-id confidential (must not be exposed in untrusted environments) and prescribes keyed derivation (sd_id128_get_machine_app_specific) for application identifiers; it is stable across reboots but clone-vulnerable (images should ship it empty) and is regenerated on re-image. Host: /etc/machine-id 0444, 32 hex; /var/lib/dbus/machine-id symlinks to it.
design_impact: host_id = keyed hash of machine-id (never the raw value) with host_id_source; label it stable-across-reboots, clone-vulnerable, not-stable-across-reimage; fall back to hashed hardware ids (NVMe wwid/eui, permanent NIC MAC) then explicit unknown; never random or time-based.

claim: DMI and EFI are firmware-platform features, not distro features: WSL2 Ubuntu has /sys/class/dmi/id and /sys/firmware/dmi ENOENT (not EACCES), no apparmor/lockdown compiled in while aa-status is installed (the inverse of the host); /sys/firmware/efi is absent on non-UEFI systems. Conversely, per sysfs(5), containers see the HOST /sys/block and /sys/class/dmi.
design_impact: ENOENT on the parent = capability absent on this platform (not-applicable), EACCES = present but restricted; tool presence and kernel capability are independent axes; establish execution context (container markers, /proc/1/cgroup, overlay root) before trusting hardware reads or a containerised run reports the host hardware as its own.

claim: kernel.dmesg_restrict=1 denies unprivileged dmesg/klogctl with EPERM (CAP_SYSLOG capability gate in check_syslog_permissions), not EACCES; /dev/kmsg is 0644 by mode yet the read fails. Host: dmesg: read kernel buffer failed: Operation not permitted. R4 stream S3 claimed EACCES; the host errno and R3 source agree on EPERM.
design_impact: Mode bits are not authorisation: record the observed errno and the policy gate value (dmesg_restrict, ptrace_scope, perf_event_paranoid, lockdown) beside the mode. EPERM (capability) and EACCES (DAC) are distinct reasons. R4-S3 EACCES claim RETRACTED (F91).

claim: errno classes carry distinct meanings and are not one-to-one with permission vs capability: protected_hardlinks denies EPERM while protected_symlinks/fifos/regular deny EACCES (fs/namei.c v6.8); a sysfs EACCES can be a write-only attribute (/sys/module/ipmi_si/parameters/hotmod is 0200); ENOENT = absent; EINVAL/ENODEV = show() rejected or device gone; EIO = backing op failed.
design_impact: Closed reason vocabulary with the syscall and path recorded beside the errno; stat() before classifying a denial; only ENOENT proven by a successful parent listing may mean feature absent.

claim: EACCES on a FILE after a successful lstat is a complete answer (exists, unreadable); EACCES on a DIRECTORY or readdir is a genuine UNKNOWN (absence unprovable); bounded finds (find / -xdev ... 2>/dev/null) silently skip other filesystems (incl. the mounted ESP) and every unreadable directory, so an empty result is a bounded negative. Host: /root, /root/.ssh, /etc/ssl/private, /etc/sudoers.d are EACCES boundaries.
design_impact: Every enumeration finding carries its scope (roots, depth, xdev, EACCES dirs count+sample, budget consumed) and is phrased none found within scope, never none exist.

claim: With kptr_restrict=1, /proc/kallsyms returns a SUCCESSFUL read of all-zero addresses to a non-root reader rather than an error.
design_impact: A third failure mode: read-succeeded-but-content-degraded. Any consumer of kernel addresses must treat all-zero as restricted, never as a value.

claim: procfs hidepid=0|1|2 (and subset=pid) changes what an unprivileged process can see of other processes. Host: /proc mounted with no hidepid option; ps saw all processes (R3-OR7).
design_impact: Read the /proc mount options from /proc/self/mountinfo before any process-enumeration conclusion; under hidepid=2 an empty enumeration is UNKNOWN.

claim: The hardening sysctls (kptr_restrict, perf_event_paranoid, unprivileged_bpf_disabled, yama/ptrace_scope, protected_*, suid_dumpable) are world-readable; ENOENT on kernel/yama/ptrace_scope means Yama is absent, not permissive. kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone is a Debian downstream knob, not semantically equal to upstream user.max_user_namespaces; WSL2 with ID=ubuntu lacks it while the host carries BOTH (unprivileged_userns_clone=1, max_user_namespaces=381532).
design_impact: Read the knob, never attempt the restricted operation; probe both userns spellings and report unknown when neither exists; capability-gate, never distro-gate. R3-F74 contested aspect resolved by host observation (both knobs present).

claim: Pseudofile st_size lies: /proc files stat 0 (cpuinfo, meminfo, self/mountinfo) and /sys attributes stat 4096 (sysfs uses a PAGE_SIZE buffer, one show() per read); but not universally: /proc/cmdline reports its real size (225) and /etc/os-release is a symlink whose lstat size is the link length (21). os.ReadFile compensates (min 512-byte buffer, grows to EOF) but is unbounded.
design_impact: Size reads from an explicit policy cap, never FileInfo.Size(); st_size 0 is not empty and 4096 is not the length; a 4096-byte cap per sysfs attribute is provably sufficient; use a bounded reader everywhere.

claim: io.LimitReader signals the cap by returning EOF, not an error, so reading exactly cap bytes makes truncation indistinguishable from a complete short answer. LOCAL_REPRO: read cap+1 and set truncated=true when written>cap.
design_impact: Canonical read primitive reads cap+1; a truncated read may never yield pass.

claim: Opening a FIFO without O_NONBLOCK blocks until a writer appears (R1 LOCAL_REPRO: cat hung the full timeout; R5 LOCAL_REPRO: os.Open blocked >700 ms while O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK returned immediately). O_NONBLOCK has no effect for regular files and block devices, so it is not a general safety net; os.Root constrains traversal but explicitly does NOT constrain object type (device files, /proc special files remain accessible). Statting the path then opening is a TOCTOU; statting the opened fd is not.
design_impact: One open path: O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK|O_CLOEXEC (O_NOFOLLOW only outside /sys and /proc), then fstat the fd and assert IsRegular before any read; lstat is an optional cheap pre-filter, not the gate. R1-F20 wording (O_NONBLOCK is not sufficient) weakened: its repro used cat, which does not set O_NONBLOCK (F95).

claim: A blocked read(2) on a regular file is not interruptible by a context: os.File.SetReadDeadline returns os.ErrNoDeadline for ordinary files (stdlib TestNonpollableDeadline asserts this on Linux).
design_impact: The whole-scan deadline bounds scheduling and output, not in-flight reads: each check runs in its own goroutine, the collector selects on ctx.Done(), emits unknown+TIMEOUT and writes findings.json without an unconditional WaitGroup.Wait().

claim: filepath.Walk/WalkDir never follow symlinks, yet /sys is built from symlinks: 28/28 /sys/block entries (WSL2) and every /sys/block entry on the host are relative symlinks (nvme0n1 -> ../devices/pci0000:00/.../nvme/nvme0/nvme0n1); /sys/class/nvme/*, /sys/class/net/*, /sys/class/dmi/id are symlinks too (R5-OR4). WalkDir has no built-in timeout or entry budget.
design_impact: Two traversal strategies: under /sys and /proc follow symlinks deliberately (os.Root or explicit depth-capped resolution with in-root assertion); under user-writable trees WalkDir with no following plus depth/entry/time budget, SkipDir on prune, SkipAll on exhaustion recorded as evidence. A blanket O_NOFOLLOW under /sys enumerates nothing.

claim: os.Root (Go 1.24+; ReadFile/Readlink 1.25) does openat-per-component within a directory, follows in-root relative symlinks and rejects escapes (LOCAL_REPRO on Go 1.26.2: OpenRoot(/sys).ReadFile(block/loop0/size) ok; Open(../etc/passwd) fails path escapes from parent; OpenRoot(/proc).ReadFile(self/status) works, 1/root/etc/passwd fails ENOTDIR unprivileged). os.DirFS is not a security boundary. Verified on kernel 6.18 WSL2, not yet on the 6.8 target.
design_impact: os.Root(/sys) and os.Root(/proc) are the production read primitives and Root.FS() the test seam; the sensor must degrade to plain bounded reads with explicit lstat gating if OpenRoot fails on the target; the IsRegular gate stays mandatory inside a Root. Supersedes R1-F21 openat2 hardening (F96).

claim: syscall.Stat_t.Dev implements xdev (distinct Dev per mount, LOCAL_REPRO and host: / 259:2 vs /boot/efi 259:1 vs /proc, /sys, /dev, /run separate). proc_pid_mountinfo(5): a VARIABLE number of optional fields precedes a literal - separator before fstype; the host root is mount 31 ext4 rw,errors=remount-ro with no overlay/bind mounts of interest (R5-OR3).
design_impact: Bounded walks compare Dev to the root Dev; mountinfo parsing splits on the literal ' - ' and indexes from both ends, never a fixed column count (a fixed-index parser silently corrupts every nosuid/nodev/network-fs verdict).

claim: exec.CommandContext default Cancel is cmd.Process.Kill, which kills only the direct child, not processes it started (os/exec source, Go 1.26.2); Setpgid alone does not give group kill.
design_impact: CommandContext alone is not a budget; the runner must set cmd.Cancel to a process-group kill.

claim: Cmd.WaitDelay (Go 1.20+, from proposal golang/go#50436 motivated by #23019; #57140 is unrelated) is the only stdlib bound on Wait when a child exits leaving pipes open or fails to exit after cancel; on expiry pipes are force-closed and Wait returns exec.ErrWaitDelay. LOCAL_REPRO: sh -c sleep 30 & echo; exit 0 blocked Output() for 30.01 s under a 3 s context with no WaitDelay, 0.21 s with WaitDelay=200ms and the 12 bytes preserved. StdoutPipe is incompatible with Run/Wait ordering.
design_impact: Every Cmd sets WaitDelay; ErrWaitDelay maps to unknown/TIMEOUT (or TRUNCATED with partial output), never fail; cap output with a limiting io.Writer on cmd.Stdout/Stderr, never StdoutPipe+LimitReader or uncapped Output().

claim: Group kill requires syscall.SysProcAttr{Setpgid:true} at Start plus syscall.Kill(-pid, SIGKILL); without Setpgid the child shares the sensor group and a negative-pid kill kills the sensor. LOCAL_REPRO (novel, single-source): WaitDelay alone left the sleep grandchild running; Setpgid+group-kill Cancel left zero survivors. A custom Cancel must normalise ESRCH to os.ErrProcessDone; exactly one Wait() per path or the child is a zombie. All needed symbols are in stdlib syscall on linux/amd64.
design_impact: One internal runner builds every exec.Cmd (Setpgid, group-kill Cancel with ESRCH normalisation, WaitDelay, capped writers, deferred Wait); a dedicated test asserts the sensor survives its own cancellation and no descendant survives. Orphan reaping (R5-F14) is single-source; re-run once on the host at implementation time.

claim: sshd -G (OpenSSH 9.6p1) dumps the effective configuration BEFORE host-key loading (sshd.c -G path :1619-1620/:1815-1816 vs key loop :1831-1936) and therefore WORKS as uid 1000: host probe printed 95 lines / 85 directives with no error (permitrootlogin without-password, passwordauthentication no, kbdinteractiveauthentication no, pubkeyauthentication yes, usepam yes, permitemptypasswords no, maxauthtries 6, listenaddress 0.0.0.0:22 and [::]:22, port 22, authorizedkeysfile, hostkey paths). The recorded rc=141 is a SIGPIPE artifact of the probe pipe (F1). sshd -T exits 1 with sshd: no hostkeys available -- exiting.
design_impact: REUSE sshd -G (bounded exec, real rc captured) as the primary in-force oracle for global sshd policy; the Include-aware parser is the fallback (sshd absent or -G fails) and the provenance/cross-check source. Note -G prints without-password for prohibit-password. Supersedes the R3/R4/contract framing that effective config can only be parsed (F97).

claim: sshd -G -C <connspec> fatals at sshd.c:1741-1747 although sshd.8:157-165 documents the combination as supported (code beats man page). NOT tested on the host (the lead probe ran -G without -C).
design_impact: Ceiling of the oracle is the GLOBAL effective config; Match-conditional policy is an explicitly bounded unknown, never folded into the global answer. Remains OPEN as an observation (OR-OPEN-1).

claim: sshd -T loads all host keys unconditionally before the test branch and exits 1 (no hostkeys available -- exiting) unprivileged because the 0600 host keys are unreadable; the man page does not document -T as requiring privilege. Host-confirmed (R3-OR8: stderr and exit 1).
design_impact: Never depend on sshd -T; if attempted, record its stderr and exit code as EXECUTION_ERROR evidence. The consequence drawn by R3/R4 (the sensor must implement its own resolver as the only path) is superseded by F24: the parser is fallback + provenance, -G is primary.

claim: sshd_config(5): for each keyword the first obtained value wins (ssh_config uses the same rule; the R3 brief assumed they were opposite); Include is expanded inline at its position, glob-sorted lexically, relative to /etc/ssh, non-fatal when nothing matches (servconf.c:2128-2215); Match blocks override the global section per connection. Host: the first non-comment line of /etc/ssh/sshd_config is Include /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf; exactly one drop-in 00-latitude-instant-deploy.conf (PasswordAuthentication no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, 0644 root) whose values the main file repeats.
design_impact: The fallback parser walks the Include chain in read order, keeps the FIRST occurrence, emits winning {path,line} and shadowed occurrences, degrades to evidence-only when a security keyword appears inside any Match block; never encode drop-ins win, encode first occurrence wins. A grep-style single-file scan reports the opposite of what is in force on hosts where the drop-in and main file disagree.

claim: OpenSSH 9.6 upstream defaults (PermitRootLogin prohibit-password, PasswordAuthentication yes, PubkeyAuthentication yes, KbdInteractiveAuthentication yes, MaxAuthTries 6, PermitEmptyPasswords no, X11Forwarding no, AllowTcpForwarding yes, LoginGraceTime 120, StrictModes yes, UsePAM no) diverge from Debian/Ubuntu packaging on UsePAM (distro default yes). On the host UsePAM is set explicitly (yes) so the divergence is moot there; generically the absent-keyword default is CONTESTED (upstream vs distro). os-release(5): key defaults off ID then ID_LIKE, never PRETTY_NAME.
design_impact: With sshd -G available the default table is only needed in the fallback path; there, every PASS from a default cites the default, its OpenSSH version and the distro family (ID/ID_LIKE); unknown distro => UNKNOWN, not the upstream default.

claim: A Match block overrides the global section for connections satisfying its criteria; per-user/host/address effective policy is not determinable statically without the connection context.
design_impact: Security keywords inside any Match block degrade the check to evidence-only (global value + enumerated conditional overrides). No Match block is present on the host.

claim: Ubuntu (22.10+) socket-activates sshd: on the host ssh.socket (ListenStream=0.0.0.0:22, [::]:22, Accept=no, FreeBind=yes, RequiredBy=ssh.service) AND ssh.service (ExecStartPre sshd -t, ExecStart sshd -D $SSHD_OPTS, KillMode=process, Type=notify) are both active, so the listening endpoint is owned by systemd. Whether the ListenStream is static or generator-derived from sshd_config Port/ListenAddress is CONTESTED generically (R4 stream S3 vs the literal unit text); the host unit shows literal ListenStream lines and the shipped sshd_config comment says socket configuration must be re-generated after changing Port/ListenAddress, so both readings can coexist (static default, generator override on change).
design_impact: Never report the SSH listen address from sshd_config alone: evidence chain = systemctl show/cat ssh.socket effective Listen -> observed listeners (/proc/net/tcp or ss) -> sshd_config/-G for auth policy; report CONTESTED when file and socket table disagree. Host-level question resolved; generic mechanism stays contested.

claim: Unprivileged ss -ltnp degrades by silent omission: exit 0, header present, Process column blank for other users sockets (inode-to-pid needs /proc/<pid>/fd gated by PTRACE_MODE_READ_FSCREDS); /proc/net/tcp{,6} is fully readable and exposes the owning uid and inode of every socket. Host: tcp/22 v4+v6 and resolved :53 listeners visible, process column empty.
design_impact: A socket listens on :22 owned by uid 0 is provable; sshd owns it is UNKNOWN+EACCES for another uid unless an independent signal (systemd unit state) is used; never read a blank ss column as evidence.

claim: Reverse tunnels (Cloudflare Tunnel, ngrok, frp) are outbound-only with no inbound listener and are structurally invisible to listening-socket enumeration; some remote-access surfaces have unprivileged non-exec signatures (WireGuard DEVTYPE=wireguard in /sys/class/net/<if>/uevent; Cockpit 9090; Tailscale UDP 41641 + tailscale0). Host: none detected.
design_impact: State the outbound-tunnel blind spot in the REMOTE_ACCESS evidence and NOTES; prefer sysfs/procfs signatures over exec; port heuristics are labelled inference.

claim: passwd -S gives L/NP/P only for the caller; /etc/shadow is 0640 root:shadow; /etc/sudoers is 0440 root:root and /etc/sudoers.d 0750 root:root on the host, so the sudo policy (incl. whether cloud-init wrote /etc/sudoers.d/90-cloud-init-users at 0440) is UNKNOWN+EACCES. The only non-empty privileged group is sudo (member ubuntu); disk, adm, systemd-journal, kmem, video, render, input, dialout, tty, shadow, kvm are EMPTY; nsswitch is files-only.
design_impact: Group membership is fact; sudo policy and other users password state are UNKNOWN+EACCES; the sensor never invokes sudo (not even sudo -n -l). Empty disk/adm/systemd-journal groups turn root:disk 0660 into root-only in practice: a reusable evidence helper.

claim: The sshd drop-in 00-latitude-instant-deploy.conf mtime (2026-09-08 17:37:29.29Z) equals ssh.service ActiveEnterTimestamp (17:37:29Z), ~22 h after boot (2026-09-07 19:29:43Z): provisioning rewrote remote-access config after boot AND restarted sshd, so the file is in force. Status raised from LIKELY on the new lead probe network.sshd_dropin_mtime_vs_boot + network.ssh_service_cat.
design_impact: A config-mtime-vs-daemon-start staleness check is meaningful (PASS here); phrase as observation, severity info: mtime is not authorship and can be set arbitrarily.

claim: No maintained Go sshd_config (server-side) parser exists: x/crypto/ssh has no config-file parser; kevinburke/ssh_config parses CLIENT config and does not support Match; a survey of six libraries found only client parsers (non-exhaustive negative). Generic traps: the Include drop-in pattern is not guaranteed on in-place-upgraded RHEL hosts; Alpine may run Dropbear with no sshd_config.
design_impact: BUILD a narrow sshd_config reader (fallback + provenance); re-verify the negative once at implementation time; detect the SSH implementation before parsing and fall back to runtime evidence for Dropbear.

claim: ufw is active on the host (systemctl is-active ufw = active); rule files (/etc/ufw/*.rules, *.init) are 0640 root:root and iptables/ufw status need root, but /etc/ufw/ufw.conf (0644) and /etc/default/ufw (0644) are readable: ENABLED= and DEFAULT_INPUT_POLICY=DROP / OUTPUT ACCEPT / FORWARD DROP are observable; nft is absent.
design_impact: Firewall check: enabled + default policies from readable config (PASS/FAIL), concrete ruleset UNKNOWN+EACCES with the observed denial strings as evidence.

claim: Secret-shaped files are classifiable from a bounded header: RFC 7468 PEM armor, OpenSSH PROTOCOL.key openssh-key-v1 with ciphername second in the header (ciphername none proves an unencrypted key within ~48 decoded bytes, key material structurally last); MIT keytab 0x0502 and JKS/JCEKS 0xFEEDFEED/0xCECECECE are LIKELY (not fetched from primary). gitleaks private-key regex must consume >=64 chars of key body, so content scanning inherently ingests key material.
design_impact: Header-only classification (<=64 bytes, classified and discarded in the same function, never stored/hashed/logged) replaces content scanning as a declared scope decision; unencrypted-private-key is obtainable with zero leak risk. JKS/keytab labels stay LIKELY.

claim: gitleaks is MIT at HEAD (v8.30.1; LICENSE unchanged since 2019-12-04) -- the R1 brief claim that it was relicensed is FALSE; it does not redact by default (--redact default 0) and serialises raw Secret and Match fields. trufflehog is AGPL-3.0 and verifies credentials against live third-party APIs by default (--no-verification is opt-out).
design_impact: REJECT both scanners on safety grounds (findings.json would become a secret-bearing artifact; outbound credential-carrying calls violate no-network), NOT on the licence myth; repeating the myth in NOTES.md would be a checkable error. Brief claim RETRACTED (F92).

claim: Several credential formats carry documented permission semantics usable as PASS/FAIL criteria: PostgreSQL ignores ~/.pgpass unless 0600 or stricter; sshd StrictModes rejects loose key-file permissions; docker config.json auths are base64, explicitly not encrypted; git-credential-store is plaintext by design.
design_impact: Cite the software own rule as the criterion rather than house style.

claim: Host secrets surface (metadata only): /run/cloud-init/instance-data.json is 0644 and self-redacting for non-root while instance-data-sensitive.json, combined-cloud-config.json and /etc/cloud/ds-identify.cfg are 0600; /boot/config-* is 0644 (build-time kernel options readable) while vmlinuz, System.map and grub.cfg are 0600; both initramfs images are 0644 (67/71 MB) and /boot/efi is mounted dmask=0022,fmask=0022 (ESP world-readable).
design_impact: Provider detection uses the world-readable file; 0600 files are reported as exists+EACCES surface, never opened; boot artefacts (initramfs commonly embeds provisioning material) are a SECRETS_ON_DISK finding by mode/size/path only; /boot/config-$(uname -r) can answer module-signing/lockdown build options where present.

claim: POSIX ACLs are decodable in pure Go from the system.posix_acl_access xattr (kernel UAPI: le32 version 0x0002 + 8-byte {le16 tag, le16 perm, le32 id} entries); R1 LOCAL_REPRO byte-verified 44 bytes = 4+8*5 on /var/log/journal decoding to group:4(adm):r-x; stdlib syscall.Getxattr/Listxattr work (R5 LOCAL_REPRO: ENODATA when no ACL). No maintained Go decoder exists (pkg/xattr raw bytes; joshlf/go-acl unpushed since 2020). xattr(7): access to system.* is filesystem-policy-defined. Host: getfacl absent; /var/log/journal shows a + (ACL present); /dev/ipmi0 and /etc/ssl/private show no +; whether getxattr succeeds on a file the caller cannot read was NOT observed (registry forbids python -c).
design_impact: BUILD a ~50-line decoder over stdlib Getxattr with a hand-built byte fixture (R5-F50 gap covered by the R1 repro but still needs a unit test); report ENODATA (no ACL) / EACCES / ENOTSUP per errno; ACL_MASK must be ANDed with USER/GROUP perms; the runtime result on the host settles OR-OPEN-2. Retires the getfacl-absent-so-UNKNOWN blocker.

claim: /dev/ipmiN is 0600 root:root because ipmi_devintf registers a class with no devnode callback and devtmpfs defaults to 0600 (ipmi_devintf.c:810-827, devtmpfs.c, core.c); there is no capable()/CAP_* gate in ipmi_devintf open() and the Debian/Ubuntu ipmitool package ships no udev rule relaxing it. Host: /dev/ipmi0 crw------- root:root 238:0; /dev/ipmidev/ absent; no ipmi udev rules or modprobe.d entries; /dev/i2c-0..2 crw------- root:root; group kmem/disk empty.
design_impact: EACCES on /dev/ipmi0 is the stock upstream default, not a Supermicro/Latitude hardening choice: report as normal posture, never as misconfiguration. Who may open it is fully determined by mode+owner+group+ACL+membership (no hidden capability gate), which makes the finding actionable. Report OBSERVED mode, never an assumed default.

claim: All BMC identity attributes under /sys/devices/platform/ipmi_bmc.N/ are 0444 (ipmi_msghandler.c:2758-2911). Host: ipmi_version=2.0, firmware_revision=1.5, manufacturer_id=0x002a7c (IANA PEN 10876 = Super Micro Computer, corroborating DMI sys_vendor independently), product_id=0x1d6e, device_id=32, guid present, provides_device_sdrs=0, additional_device_support=0xbf; /sys/class/ipmi/ipmi0 dev 238:0, modalias acpi:IPI0001.
design_impact: The BMC_INBAND_ACCESS identity answer without touching the device node; compare IPMI manufacturer vs DMI vendor as an agree/disagree consistency observation, never gate on a vendor value. No prior art found uses this path.

claim: Reading the 0444 BMC sysfs attributes is not a passive dump: device_id_show -> bmc_get_device_id issues a live Get Device ID over KCS whenever the short dynamic cache (IPMI_DYN_DEV_ID_EXPIRY) has expired; KCS timeouts are 5 s IBF + 5 s OBF with up to 10 retries (ipmi_kcs_sm.c:103-106, IPMI v2.0 s9.20), so a wedged BMC can block read() for tens of seconds and a goroutine cannot be cancelled mid-syscall. The guid attribute exists only when the kernel actually obtained one (ipmi_msghandler.c:2941-2946). Host timing (healthy BMC): device_id 1.41 ms, firmware_revision 1.63 ms, device_id again 0.98 ms.
design_impact: Non-zero self-consistent values plus a present guid prove the BMC ANSWERED a read-only identification (the category anchor check), obtained unprivileged with no ipmitool and no device open. The read needs an out-of-band deadline (own goroutine + timer, result abandoned on overrun, unknown/TIMEOUT), not a naive context; state that the inference is from driver behaviour, not a request the sensor issued. Both R1 and R4 read the same primary (kernel source), so this is one source plus host observation.

claim: Kernel IPMI split (Documentation/driver-api/ipmi.rst): ipmi_msghandler (no user interface), ipmi_devintf (/dev/ipmiN ioctl), ipmi_si (KCS/SMIC/BT), ipmi_ssif (SMBus); interfaces are auto-discovered from ACPI/SMBIOS or hand-configured via module params or the write-only hotmod parameter; IPMB commands time out after 5 s with a generated response; SMBus discovery can disturb I2C peers. The chrdev registers the name ipmidev (never ipmi0) in /proc/devices. Host: ipmi_si bound to ACPI IPI0001 (\_SB_.PCI0.SBRG.SIKC) + dmi-ipmi-si.0, refcount 1; ipmi_devintf use count 0 (nothing has /dev/ipmi0 open); acpi_ipmi, ipmi_ssif loaded; in-band KCS is functional at driver level.
design_impact: Model BMC_INBAND_ACCESS as separable checks: firmware declares interface (DMI 38-0 dir), driver bound and BMC identified (sysfs), who may open the node (mode/ACL/groups), latent host interface (USB gadget) -- pass+info+fail instead of one unknown. Never issue an IPMI command; hotmod EACCES is expected; /proc/devices must be grepped for ipmidev. A TIMEOUT is never no BMC.

claim: Mature BMC prior art fails unprivileged: ipmitool overwrites errno across /dev/ipmi0, /dev/ipmi/0, /dev/ipmidev/0 and reports EACCES as ENOENT; u-root/pkg/ipmi (and bougou/go-ipmi, vmware/goipmi) open the node O_RDWR; osquery has no IPMI table (2017 attempt closed unmerged). No unprivileged path exists on the host to BMC LAN config, users or channel privileges (root-only node, no client tool).
design_impact: BUILD the category (steal ipmitool path list, invert control flow, retain errno per path); who can reach the BMC over the network is UNKNOWN with reason naming EACCES + missing client; never substitute the weaker we saw a BMC NIC answer.

claim: DMTF DSP0270 v1.3.1 defines SMBIOS type 42 (Redfish host interface) with device type 02h/04h = USB network interface sourcing idVendor/idProduct/iSerialNumber from the USB descriptors; its Get Bootstrap Account Credentials operation CREATES a BMC account (a write). Host: USB NIC enx... = Linux 5.4.62 with aspeed_vhub / RNDIS/Ethernet Gadget 0b1f:03ee, operstate DOWN, no address; Supermicro documents the H13SRE-F/AS-3015MR-H10TNR with an ASPEED AST2600 BMC (IPMI 2.0, Redfish, dedicated IPMI LAN port) consistent with the AST1150 bridge and ASPEED VGA on PCI. The dedicated out-of-band LAN port is invisible to the OS, so R2-F17 (BMC not network-reachable at scan time) over-claims.
design_impact: Report the latent Redfish host interface as INFO from the USB descriptor surface (a verdict, not UNKNOWN); out-of-band exposure is outside the observation boundary and must be stated as UNKNOWN, never as unreachable; Redfish bootstrap and every ipmitool set/chassis/user subcommand are on the permanent do-not-run list. R2-F17 RETRACTED as stated (F93).

claim: /sys/firmware/efi/efivars is world-readable (the older /sys/firmware/efi/vars is root-only; osquery chose efivars because not requiring root outweighs the format) and each variable file carries 4 bytes of little-endian UEFI attributes BEFORE the data. Host: SecureBoot = 06 00 00 00 | 00 and SetupMode = 06 00 00 00 | 01, and mokutil --sb-state agrees: Secure Boot DISABLED, platform in Setup Mode (two independent unprivileged paths). osquery secureboot silently emits no row on read failure.
design_impact: Read 5 bytes and take index 4 (byte 0 gives the wrong answer confidently); mokutil is an optional cross-check, never the mechanism; Setup Mode (no PK enrolled, anyone with firmware access can enrol keys) is the more severe fact and deserves its own check; efivars absent = not-applicable (BIOS), distinct from disabled; one finding per check by construction (never osquery silent omission).

claim: /proc/sys/kernel/tainted is world-readable; bit 12 (4096) = O out-of-tree, bit 13 (8192) = E unsigned; host 12288 = O+E attributable to exactly one module via /sys/module/bnxt_en/taint = OE (the only non-empty /sys/module/*/taint).
design_impact: Embed the kernel bit table as data so evidence reads as a decode; attribute per module via /sys/module/*/taint; gate on letters, never a module-name list; E records an unsigned module even when signatures are not enforced (do not infer enforcement from taint).

claim: /sys/kernel/security/lsm is the documented comma-separated active-LSM list (host: lockdown,capability,landlock,yama,apparmor); the Lockdown LSM (5.4+) exposes /sys/kernel/security/lockdown (host: -rw-r--r-- root:root, value [none] integrity confidentiality); securityfs itself is dr-xr-xr-x/drwxr-xr-x and traversable, ENOENT on WSL2 (no LSM exposed) -- so the S5 briefing assumption securityfs is root-only was wrong. AppArmor: /sys/module/apparmor/parameters/enabled = Y, but /sys/kernel/security/apparmor/profiles is 0444 AND returns EACCES (apparmorfs policy), and parameters/mode is EACCES; aa-status absent. R4-F44 (profiles readable without root) is REFUTED by the host.
design_impact: Enumerate LSMs from /sys/kernel/security/lsm; ENOENT = not mounted/no LSM framework (unknown, never no LSMs); lockdown ENOENT on <5.4 = feature absent, on 5.4+ = LSM not enabled (different reasons). AppArmor enforcement mode is UNKNOWN BY CONSTRUCTION unprivileged on this host; only enabled=Y is positive evidence. R4-F44 RETRACTED (F94); R4-F18 resolved as unknown-by-construction.

claim: /sys/devices/system/cpu/vulnerabilities/* are 0444, one file per vulnerability, and the file SET is kernel-version dependent (recent kernels add ghostwrite, indirect_target_selection). Host: all Not affected or mitigated.
design_impact: Enumerate the directory rather than hardcoding a list, or the check silently under-reports on other kernels.

claim: Kernel drift is provable unprivileged: running 6.8.0-139-generic (uname, /proc/cmdline BOOT_IMAGE) while /boot/vmlinuz and initrd.img symlink to 7.0.0-31-generic, vmlinuz.old to the running one, /lib/modules holds both; /var/run/reboot-required is ENOENT and update-notifier-common (which creates it) can simply be absent (WSL repro), so its absence is never evidence. /var/lib/apt/lists is EMPTY and update-success-stamp is absent, so apt list --upgradable printing nothing means nothing.
design_impact: Drift check compares uname with the boot-directory default; a patch-currency check must first verify apt metadata exists and is fresh, else unknown (reason: package index empty/stale) -- the single strongest false-negative trap in an Update/Drift category on this host.

claim: sd_booted(3): systemd-is-PID1 test is the existence of /run/systemd/system (not systemctl presence or /proc/1/comm). systemd-detect-virt exits 0 when virtualization IS detected and non-zero when none (host: none, rc=1 = bare metal; corroborated by DMI, BMC, TPM). util-linux JSON output (-J) exists only from 2.27.
design_impact: Capability gates before probes: systemd path test (unknown, not fail, when absent); detect-virt keyed on stdout token + documented polarity, UTILITY_MISSING = unknown not bare metal, corroborate with a second signal (DMI strings are attacker-settable); never assume -J, never positional column parsing.

claim: os-release(5): only ID (default linux), NAME, PRETTY_NAME have defaults; VERSION_ID and ID_LIKE may be absent from a well-formed file; /etc/os-release takes precedence over /usr/lib/os-release without merging; PRETTY_NAME is display-only. Host: /etc/os-release is a symlink to /usr/lib/os-release; ID=ubuntu VERSION_ID=24.04.
design_impact: Missing VERSION_ID = unknown, not parse failure; no merging; distro-family conditionals key off ID then ID_LIKE; legacy release files only as corroboration.

claim: /sys/block/<dev>/size is DEVICE_ATTR 0444 printing bdev_nr_sectors() in fixed 512-byte units regardless of logical_block_size (block/genhd.c v6.8; undocumented in Documentation/ABI/stable/sysfs-block for v6.8). Host arithmetic: 1875385008 x 512 = 960,197,124,096 bytes = nvme list capacity.
design_impact: size_bytes = size x 512 unconditionally, never x logical_block_size (identical here, wrong by 8x on a 4Kn device: needs a fixture). TASK_CONTRACT B5a wording (x logical block size 512) must be corrected (F99).

claim: NVMe identity is world-readable sysfs (drivers/nvme/host/sysfs.c S_IRUGO: model, serial, firmware_rev, cntlid, transport, state, subsysnqn; namespace wwid/nguid/uuid/nsid flat under /sys/block/nvmeXnY/, NOT under a nvme/ subdir; no Documentation/ABI file exists for the NVMe class). nvme list (nvme-cli 2.8) reads sysfs, not ioctls. Device-name prefixes do not classify transport (Hyper-V synthetic disks are sd*). Host: two Micron_7450_MTFDKCC960TFR, fw E2MU200, pcie, state live.
design_impact: Storage identity straight from sysfs with no nvme-cli dependency; classify transport from driver links/PCI class/nvme class membership, never from names; fixtures model the flat namespace layout.

claim: lsblk(8) reads sysfs and the udev database and only probes devices directly when udev data is unavailable (blkid is authoritative); blkid as uid 1000 prints nothing and exits 0. The world-readable udev DB /run/udev/data/b<maj>:<min> (host: 0755, 362 entries; b259:0 has ID_MODEL, ID_SERIAL_SHORT, ID_WWN, ID_REVISION, ID_PART_TABLE_TYPE=gpt, by-id links) supplies model/serial/WWN/fstype/UUID without opening the device; host lsblk populated FSTYPE (vfat/ext4), MODEL, SERIAL, WWN, TRAN=nvme for both drives as uid 1000 although /dev/nvme*n1 is root:disk 0660 with disk empty, which proves the udev path. The fallback is partial (UUID null for 2 of 4 WSL devices).
design_impact: Never shell out to blkid; read udev data (primary) with sysfs fallback; reporting fstype/identity as UNKNOWN when udev answers is under-claiming, but an EMPTY field is unknown, never no filesystem -- phrase nvme1n1 as no filesystem signature known to udev. Serial-bearing fields are identity-sensitive in evidence. Status carried from R3-F46b (VERIFIED); R4-F08 (LIKELY) is subsumed by the host proof.

claim: dm-crypt/LUKS mappings are identifiable unprivileged by the CRYPT- prefix of /sys/block/dm-*/dm/uuid (cryptsetup libdevmapper.c:1163-1189). Host: /dev/mapper holds only control, no /dev/dm-*, no /etc/lvm/lvm.conf, FSTYPE vfat/ext4 -- dm-crypt provably ABSENT. TCG Opal/SED state has zero sysfs exposure (block/sed-opal.c gates every ioctl on CAP_SYS_ADMIN) and the Micron MTFDKCC960TFR base part number is shared by non-SED and SED SKUs (LIKELY 0.6, datasheet unfetched); ext4 fscrypt is kernel-supported (features/encryption) but whether the fs uses it needs the superblock -- UNKNOWN unprivileged.
design_impact: Encryption-at-rest finding = fail (or info) scoped to dm-crypt/LUKS with the SED and fscrypt blind spots named in the reason; no CRYPT- uuid means no dm-crypt, never not encrypted; SED capability is never inferred from the model string.

claim: NVMe SMART/health needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN: nvme_cmd_allowed() (drivers/nvme/host/ioctl.c:85) gates admin passthrough; /dev/nvme0 (char) is 0600 root:root by default udev rules while /dev/nvme0n1* (block) are root:disk 0660 -- so joining group disk would NOT grant SMART (R4-F04 remediation corrected by R4-F54). Host: nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1 -> Permission denied rc=1; nvme id-ctrl -> Permission denied; smartctl absent; group disk empty. Surviving health signal: /sys/fs/ext4/nvme0n1p2/errors_count=0, first_error_*, lifetime_write_kbytes readable.
design_impact: Drive health = unknown with reason requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN on the NVMe character device; no unprivileged path exists (never requires group disk, never smartctl not installed); identity is still reported (not unknown); ext4 errors_count is the partial signal. R4-F04 remediation wording RETRACTED (F100).

claim: No storage redundancy on the host, provable unprivileged: /proc/mdstat shows Personalities loaded but unused devices: <none> (md_seq_show keeps Personalities populated whenever personalities are loaded, so proof needs no md<N> lines + unused: none), /dev/md* ENOENT, no dm target, PCI storage classes are 0108 (NVM) and 0106 (AHCI ASM1061 with 12 empty scsi_hosts) with no 0104 RAID controller; nvme1n1 has no partition table, no filesystem signature, no holders.
design_impact: High-confidence finding: root filesystem has no redundancy while a second identical unused device is installed; the redundancy check is a three-signal rule (never the Personalities line alone; a RAID-named AHCI controller is not RAID).

claim: queue/write_cache (host: write through) describes the block layer cache-flush behaviour, not power-loss protection or durability.
design_impact: Report write_cache as an observed setting, severity info; never translate into a data-integrity claim.

claim: Installed RAM (memory blocks x block size) and kernel-visible MemTotal differ materially (R1 LOCAL_REPRO: 63 x 128 MiB = 8064 MiB vs MemTotal 7721 MiB). Host MemTotal 97938032 kB, no swap.
design_impact: memory_bytes = MemTotal x 1024 with memory_source naming the file; installed capacity is a separate labelled extra; never let one stand in for the other.

claim: ghw converts any DMI read error incl. EACCES into the untyped string unknown with no errno (pkg/linuxdmi via util.UNKNOWN), scrapes /var/log/syslog for installed RAM and silently substitutes usable RAM when that fails (the host user is not in adm), and exposes a PRODUCTION chroot override (WithChroot + GHW_CHROOT env); its README claims no root needed (l.14) while documenting permission warnings (l.1045-1051). gopsutil bakes HOST_PROC/HOST_SYS/HOST_ETC env overrides into the library and HostID() returns an empty string with nil error on total failure. zcalusic/sysinfo requires superuser and its example log.Fatal()s unprivileged.
design_impact: REJECT ghw, gopsutil, sysinfo as dependencies (errno destruction, silent substitution, ambient env root override = attack surface in a security sensor, empty-string ids forbidden by the brief, process abort); STEAL their patterns (per-domain packages, host-id ladder, udev route, explicit-unknown sentinel). A README claim about unprivileged behaviour must be checked against code (CR-3).

claim: prometheus/procfs sysfs/class_dmi.go models every DMI field as *string, reads regular files only, and has an explicit os.IsPermission -> continue branch (Only root is allowed to read the serial and product_uuid files).
design_impact: The one library modelling unprivileged DMI correctly; pointer-or-nil is the Go shape for explicit unknown. STEAL_PATTERN (a thin wrapper would still be needed to record which errno produced the nil; importing a large surface to save ~150 LOC is not justified -- R5 IMPL_BVB row 1; C-33).

claim: osquery is dual-licensed Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-only (consumer chooses); its disk_encryption table returns ZERO rows non-root (indistinguishable from nothing encrypted) and secureboot emits no row on read failure. Wazuh SCA sshd rules are all c:sshd -T with no unknown state (false FAILs unprivileged) and SCA documents one not applicable label for absent/unreadable/timeout. Lynis (GPLv3) skips with a SKIPREASON taxonomy (include/functions:2707-2764). CIS marks recommendations Automated/Manual (LIKELY). Lynis-degradation and FreeIPMI (GPLv3) are behaviour references only.
design_impact: Three mature tools commit the exact critical failure the brief names (silent omission, errno clobber, false FAIL): citable NOTES.md contrast and the strongest argument that UNKNOWN semantics are the engineering content. Steal Lynis taxonomy as the reason vocabulary shape (idea only, GPLv3); learn from osquery under the Apache arm; never link osquery (C++/CGO).

claim: XCCDF 1.2 (NIST IR 7275 r4, confirmed against the NIST XSD) defines nine rule results (pass, fail, error, unknown, notapplicable, notchecked, notselected, informational, fixed); OVAL six (true, false, unknown, error, not evaluated, not applicable); SARIF 2.1.0 result.kind (notApplicable, pass, fail, review, open, informational) defaults to fail when omitted and separates run-level invocation status from results. R1 could only reach a NIST landing page (LIKELY); R3 fetched the XSD.
design_impact: Our pass|fail|unknown collapses error/unknown/notapplicable/notchecked: recover them in a closed reason vocabulary; one finding per registered check always; an unset verdict must never default to the safe answer; sensor-level problems belong in a run-level structure distinct from findings. R1-F57 subsumed.

claim: NIST SP 800-115 is the intended citation for absence-of-a-finding is not absence-of-the-condition, but its PDF text layer resisted extraction; no quotable sentence obtained.
design_impact: Supports no law; the doctrine is grounded in F66 instead. Follow-up needs a PDF-capable extractor.

claim: node_exporter uses a static factory-map registry with per-file init() self-registration, isolates collectors only against RETURNED errors (no recover(), no per-collector deadline, unbounded goroutine fan-out) and separates ErrNoData from failure; osquery-go registers tables as typed metadata + GenerateFunc; kube-bench separates YAML definitions from the Go runner; go.dev/doc/modules/layout endorses cmd/ + internal/ and golang-standards/project-layout states it is not official.
design_impact: Fixed Registry built at start from explicit Register(check) calls with metadata as Go struct literals (no YAML DSL, no reflection); per-check recover() and deadlines are OUR addition (node_exporter is not evidence they are unnecessary); tri-state result with UNKNOWN never collapsed into FAIL; cmd/sensor + internal/*.

claim: santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 v6.0.3 (Apache-2.0, released 2026-08-06) supports draft-04/06/07/2019-09/2020-12, defaults to 2020-12 when $schema is absent, and scores 100% on Bowtie (1301/1301 on 2020-12, 1261/1261 on 2019-09, 929/929 on draft-07, recomputed from the raw 2026-09-08 run) with one production dependency (golang.org/x/text; measured: 2 modules, 15 linked packages). xeipuuv/gojsonschema v1.2.0 is draft-07-max with 874/929 and 20 hard errors, 2018 pins, last real commit 2020; kaptinlin silently bumps the toolchain to go 1.27 and pulls YAML+i18n+uuid; qri-io is dormant; only santhosh and xeipuuv have Bowtie harnesses.
design_impact: Validator = santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 v6.0.3, decided on measured conformance; the derived schema declares 2020-12 so the default-draft hazard (R1-OR1) is moot; enable format assertion for date-time; validate the real findings.json at the release gate.

claim: A package imported only from _test.go files is not in go list -deps for main and is not linked into the binary (R1). R5 argues runtime validation of the marshalled document before writing is the only strategy that protects the delivered artifact (LIKELY 0.8) and proposes write nothing + exit 1 on failure. task/original/finding.schema.json never existed; the derived task/derived/finding.schema.json (2020-12, additionalProperties open, reason required for fail/unknown, integers for cores/memory_bytes/size_bytes) is now the fixed validation source, which makes schema-shape drift a compile-time/test-time property and makes codegen an optional extra only.
design_impact: Reconciled recommendation (C-06): full-schema validation is a TEST-time obligation (test-only import, not linked) plus the lead release gate on the real findings.json; the shipped binary enforces the same ~10 constraints as stdlib invariants (required fields non-empty, enums, reason present on fail/unknown, unique check_id, RFC 3339 parse, integers) and NEVER suppresses output on failure (write the file, exit non-zero, print pointers to stderr) because no output is worse than a flagged invalid output (D3). Reversal: if Lava sends a richer real schema, revisit runtime full validation. R5-F51 superseded by AM-1 settlement (F101).

claim: golang.org/x/sys v0.48.0 is BSD-3, pure Go, zero transitive deps and supplies Getxattr, Statfs, Openat2, Faccessat, Ioctl, Uname (R1). But every symbol the sensor needs -- SysProcAttr.Setpgid, Kill, SIGKILL, Stat_t.Dev, Getxattr, Listxattr, Statfs/Statfs_t.Flags -- exists in frozen stdlib syscall on linux/amd64 and was exercised in R5 LOCAL_REPRO; src/syscall/syscall.go carries a package NOTE preferring x/sys but no symbol is godoc-Deprecated. Openat2 is the only x/sys-exclusive item and R1 itself classes it as optional hardening while os.Root (R3-F18, F19) provides containment without it. GOOS=linux cross-doc is required on the Windows workstation.
design_impact: Resolved (C-05): stdlib syscall only, zero runtime third-party dependencies; x/sys REJECTED for this deliverable with reversal condition (statx, openat2 flags, netlink, second GOOS). R1 x/sys facts remain true; its REUSE verdict is retracted (F102).

claim: encoding/json v1 sorts map keys and preserves struct field order (LOCAL_REPRO); json.Marshal HTML-escapes < > & unless Encoder.SetEscapeHTML(false); Encode appends a newline; time.Time marshals as RFC3339Nano with trimmed zeros (variable width); floats use shortest-round-trip and may render exponents. encoding/json/v2 is GOEXPERIMENT-gated in Go 1.26 and marshals maps NON-deterministically unless Deterministic is set.
design_impact: Ship on encoding/json v1 (hard constraint for D8 determinism): Encoder with SetEscapeHTML(false)+SetIndent, explicit t.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339) strings, int64 for every count/size/mode/uid/exit code, findings sorted by (category, check_id).

claim: GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build on Windows (Go 1.26.2) produced a statically linked ELF that ran as uid 1000 under WSL (four repro binaries); with cgo off os/user parses /etc/passwd directly and net uses the pure-Go resolver; -trimpath strips workstation paths and ReadBuildInfo exposes VCS stamps; Windows filesystems carry no execute bit so tar records whatever mode the stat emulation reports (LIKELY).
design_impact: Cross-compile static (host has no Go); build the tarball with explicit 0755 on the binary and document chmod +x; --version from ReadBuildInfo with -ldflags -X fallback; user/group findings state their source as /etc/passwd parsed in-process (incomplete on LDAP/SSSD hosts).

claim: flag.NewFlagSet + a switch on os.Args[1] covers sensor scan --out, --version, help in ~20 lines (ExitOnError exits 2 on bad flags); spf13/cobra requires four external modules (go-md2man, mousetrap, pflag, yaml/v3); trivy --exit-code conflating findings with process failure is a documented wart; sysexits.h reserves 64 for usage.
design_impact: No CLI framework. Exit policy: 0 = scan completed and file written (whatever the pass/fail/unknown mix), 1 = could not complete or write, 2 = usage error; never severity-dependent.

claim: testing/fstest.MapFS supports symlink entries in current Go (LIKELY; must be proven by one test given 100% of /sys/block is symlinks); the go tool ignores testdata/; the -update golden idiom is convention not stdlib; testing/synctest (GA 1.25) virtualises time for concurrency tests, not output stamping, and GOEXPERIMENT=synctest no longer exists in 1.26; T.Setenv forbids parallel tests.
design_impact: Test seams: fs.FS parameter receiving Root.FS() in production and a fixture FS in tests (unexported, never an env var), injected runner interface, injected now func; golden findings.json reviewed by a human; PATH-shim tests non-parallel.

claim: lavahq.io and lavalabs.io are one company (301 redirect; GitHub org lava-security-research lists lavahq.io and research@lavalabs.io): a pre-launch (Coming soon) ISO 27001-certified security company positioned as Security for Enterprise Data Centers and Neoclouds, built by infrastructure engineers and security experts focused on the layers hardest to manage, secure and control. Same-named unrelated companies (an AI-payments Lava with lava.breezy.hr and $5.8M; Lava Network blockchain ~$27M; Lava International; Lavastorm; etc.) were actively surfaced by search and excluded; no funding data attributable to lavahq.io was found.
design_impact: Identity anchor for all Lava facts; no payments/blockchain facts may be attributed to Lava; funding is genuinely unknown (absence of evidence for a stealth company).

claim: None of the 17 pages reached in a sitemap-complete crawl of lavahq.io (17/18 URLs) contain the brief phrasing tens of thousands / central plane / no way in, only a way out; the only public repo (forge-framework) is Markdown + images with no code or stack signal; no careers page or ATS exists (only we are scaling fast... always looking for top-tier talent).
design_impact: The brief fleet/one-way-out framing is unverified from the public web (silence, not contradiction); public evidence gives Lava risk taxonomy, not engineering stack; hiring-stack signal is a gap, not a guess.

claim: Lava flagship research (~2026-07-28) scanned the internet and found 36,872 exposed IPMI/BMC hosts on UDP/623, 24,650 (66.9%) leaking password-derived RAKP hashes pre-login via CVE-2013-4786, mapped as BMCRadar, responsibly disclosed to Supermicro and HPE; independently corroborated by CSOonline (differently-owned source).
design_impact: Supports ranking BMC posture highly; on this host the sensor reports posture, not exposure (F47).

claim: FORGE (github lava-security-research/forge-framework, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, 20 stars; authors Michael Katchinskiy, Head of Security Research, and Yakir Kadkoda, CTO/co-founder; reviewers from Google, Dell, Nebius, Roblox, IBM, Intel, Visa) has five pillars: Fleet Integrity, Operations & Management Planes, Resource Isolation, Grid, Evidence & Exposure Management (defined around provider transparency and patch velocity). The Breaking the Trust series covers chain of trust, SPDM/CoRIM, MoonBounce/LoJax/BlackLotus/iLOBleed/MegaRAC/CosmicStrand and attestation over self-report; the runtime-integrity series names kernel rootkits, eBPF backdoors, LD_PRELOAD, module signing, lockdown, eBPF restriction and continuous verification.
design_impact: Secure Boot/Setup Mode, TPM, taint/unsigned modules, lockdown and hardening sysctls are exactly the classes Lava own research treats as foundational (Fleet Integrity); patch velocity supports a drift/staleness angle. All 17 lavahq.io pages are ONE independence class (same vendor); FORGE repo is the same org.

claim: Lava neocloud/shared-responsibility posts name storage media sanitization, hardware and device lifecycle... reuse, decommissioning, GPU state cleanup between workloads, ask how is shared storage isolated and what happens to a bare-metal machine before it moves from one customer to another.
design_impact: Direct textual support for a storage-reuse / data-remanence / decommissioning-hygiene angle; the leap to a specific NVMe-health check is inference, not a verified claim.

claim: Lava frames its readers as data-center operators, neocloud/GPU-cloud providers and CISOs/infrastructure leadership, and its own writing cites CVE ids, quantifies numerically, names vendors and disclosure timelines, and states ethical/scope boundaries explicitly (We did not submit the matching passwords...).
design_impact: Evidence strings should be concrete (paths, exit codes, errno) and boundary-explicit (what was NOT done: no writes, no auth attempts, no IPMI commands). Inference about findings.json consumption, not a public statement.

claim: TPM 2.0 is present on the host (/sys/class/tpm/tpm0 -> platform MSFT0101:00, tpm_version_major 2) with /dev/tpm0 and /dev/tpmrm0 0600 root:root; PCR values and the event log (/sys/kernel/security/tpm0/binary_bios_measurements) are expected root-only.
design_impact: TPM presence is proven; TPM usage/measured-boot state is UNKNOWN+EACCES, never no measured boot.

claim: Host platform: Latitude.sh bare metal (cloud-init EC2-style datasource, facility CHI, hostname f4-metal-small-chi-1, Latitude drop-in), Supermicro AS -3015MR-H10TNR / H13SRE-F v1.01 / BIOS 2.4a 2025-08-29 (AMI), AMD EPYC 4484PX 12c/24t SMT, MemTotal 97938032 kB, no swap, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 6.8.0-139-generic (7.0.0-31 installed), systemd, 355 packages, uid 1000 ubuntu in groups ubuntu sudo, no Go toolchain, gcc/make/tar/curl/rsync present.
design_impact: Deep branches for what this host has (NVMe, ext4+vfat ESP, systemd socket-activated sshd, ufw, AppArmor, TPM 2.0, IPMI KCS + USB RNDIS gadget, UEFI without Secure Boot, cloud-init); generic fallbacks + UNKNOWN elsewhere; cross-compile static linux/amd64.

claim: Ubuntu 24.04 cloud images typically ship /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/50-cloud-init.conf (driven by cloud-init ssh_pwauth) which, with the Include at the top, overrides a later PasswordAuthentication in the main file. NOT present on this host (only 00-latitude-instant-deploy.conf).
design_impact: Discover drop-in filenames by listing, never assume; the law rests on F27 (primary), not on this.

claim: sysfs(5): for sysfs in the initial namespace all devices propagate into all non-initial namespaces, so an ordinary container sees the host block devices and DMI identity (corroborated by runtime issue reports).
design_impact: Largest cross-machine false-positive trap: establish execution context (container markers, /proc/1/cgroup, mountinfo overlay root) before hardware inventory and annotate/downgrade findings when containerised.

claim: RETRACTED: mdadm.conf is absent on the host (earlier state/HOST_SNAPSHOT.json prose and HOST_SUMMARY). Reason: probe storage.mdadm_conf printed HOMEHOST <ignore> (the content of /etc/mdadm/mdadm.conf); only /etc/mdadm.conf is ENOENT; R4-F02 evidence wins; lead corrected the artifacts 23:08Z.
design_impact: Replaced by F2.

claim: RETRACTED: dmesg_restrict denials surface as EACCES (R4 stream S3). Reason: host stderr is Operation not permitted (EPERM) and kernel/printk/printk.c check_syslog_permissions is a CAP_SYSLOG capability check (R3-F03).
design_impact: Replaced by F8; reason strings must quote the observed errno, never a documented one.

claim: RETRACTED: gitleaks was relicensed away from MIT (R1 brief premise). Reason: MIT at HEAD v8.30.1; LICENSE file has three commits, newest 2019-12-04 (R1-F14).
design_impact: Replaced by F38; gitleaks is rejected for redaction/serialisation reasons only.

claim: RETRACTED as stated: this host BMC is not network-reachable at scan time (R2-F17, LIKELY 0.7). Reason: the OS sees only the in-band KCS path and a DOWN USB host interface; Supermicro documents a dedicated out-of-band IPMI LAN port on this board that the OS cannot observe (R4-F53), so network reachability is UNKNOWN by construction, not absent.
design_impact: Replaced by F47; affects R2 CUSTOM_CATEGORY_CANDIDATES #3 rationale (see PROPAGATION_AUDIT).

claim: RETRACTED: /sys/kernel/security/apparmor/profiles is 0444 and therefore AppArmor profile enumeration is readable without root (R4-F44). Reason: host probe kernel.apparmor_profiles shows mode -r--r--r-- AND cat: Permission denied (apparmorfs policy check); mode bits are not authorisation (R4-F12).
design_impact: Replaced by F50; AppArmor enforcement mode is UNKNOWN by construction unprivileged on this host.

claim: RETRACTED as stated: lstat-first is mandatory and O_NONBLOCK is not sufficient (R1-F20). Reason: the R1 repro used cat, which does not set O_NONBLOCK; R5 LOCAL_REPRO showed O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK open of a FIFO returns immediately (R5-F24) and R3-F17 shows statting the path before open is a TOCTOU -- the gate is fstat on the opened fd. lstat remains a valid cheap pre-filter.
design_impact: Replaced by F16.

claim: RETRACTED as design: openat2(RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS) as optional hardening behind ENOSYS detection (R1-F21; R1 BVB row). Reason: os.Root provides kernel-enforced containment with in-root symlink following at zero dependency (R5-F22) and R3-F18 concludes the project should not reach for openat2 or x/sys for safety os.Root does not provide; the fact about openat2 needing 5.6+ stays true but unused.
design_impact: Replaced by F19.

claim: RETRACTED as framing: effective sshd policy cannot be obtained from sshd itself unprivileged, so the sensor must implement its own Include/Match walker as the primary mechanism (R3-F23 design_impact, R4-F19, TASK_CONTRACT C4a). Reason: sshd -G works as uid 1000 on the host (F24); the parser is the fallback and provenance source. The underlying fact about sshd -T stands (F26).
design_impact: Replaced by F24/F26. TASK_CONTRACT C4a was already updated by the lead (sshd -G primary); R3 DESIGN_LAWS L18 (own walker is primary), R4 HOST_SPECIFIC_PLAN B2.4 (do not shell out to sshd), R4 GENERIC_FALLBACK_PLAN s7, R4 REPORT s2.3 still carry the stale framing (PROPAGATION_AUDIT).

claim: SUPERSEDED: only raw under /sys/firmware/dmi/entries/<n>-<m>/ is root-only (R4-F30 phrasing). Reason: R4-F49 (kernel v6.8 source) and host probe bmc.dmi_entry_attrs show every attribute (handle, instance, length, position, raw, type) is 0400.
design_impact: Replaced by F4.

claim: STALE WORDING: size_bytes = /sys/block/<d>/size x logical block size 512 (TASK_CONTRACT B5a). Reason: the unit is a fixed 512-byte sector independent of logical_block_size (F55); multiplying by logical_block_size is wrong on 4Kn devices.
design_impact: Replaced by F55; lead to correct B5a.

claim: RETRACTED (remediation only): SMART is unreachable because the account is not in group disk (R4-F04 design_impact). Reason: the admin passthrough goes through the 0600 root:root character device and nvme_cmd_allowed() requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN (R4-F54, R3-F48); group disk would not help. The EACCES observation itself stands.
design_impact: Replaced by F59.

claim: SUPERSEDED: finding.schema.json is not present and schema-shape decisions are deferred (R5-F51; R1-OR1/OR8; R5-OR1). Reason: AM-1 settled by the user on 2026-09-09 -- no separate file was ever supplied; the brief contract was transcribed into task/derived/finding.schema.json (draft 2020-12, additionalProperties open, reason required for fail/unknown, integers for cores/memory_bytes/size_bytes, format date-time needs assertion).
design_impact: Replaced by F69/F70; every when the real schema arrives / not yet in hand clause in R1/R5 artifacts is stale (PROPAGATION_AUDIT). CLAUDE.md line 8 and TASK_CONTRACT AM-1 already reflect the derived schema; TASK_CONTRACT B6/B7/H-table still carry PENDING-SCHEMA tags.

claim: RETRACTED (verdict only): golang.org/x/sys is the one runtime dependency worth taking / REUSE shipped (R1 BVB_MATRIX, R1 REPORT). Reason: every needed symbol exists in stdlib syscall and was exercised (R5-F15/F26/F28); the only x/sys-exclusive item (Openat2) is dropped with F96. The x/sys facts (licence, footprint) stay true.
design_impact: Replaced by F71.

claim: RETRACTED: /sys/kernel/security is root-only (R1 stream S5 briefing assumption). Reason: LOCAL_REPRO dr-xr-xr-x traversable (R1-F36) and host kernel.securityfs_modes drwxr-xr-x with lockdown 0644 and lsm 0444.
design_impact: Replaced by F50.

claim: CONTESTED (contract vs research): TASK_CONTRACT AM-6/C6a permit running ipmitool mc info (Get Device ID) as a read when the device node is openable, with a hard timeout. Research position: never issue an IPMI command at all -- the sysfs identity path yields the same payload unprivileged with less hang risk (R1 BVB: in-band Get Device ID via ioctl REJECT for our host and do not implement generically; R3 L26), and IPMI discovery paths have documented bus-disturbance risk (R3-F42). Moot on this host (node not openable); a real design choice generically.
design_impact: Recommendation: adopt the research position (no IPMI commands ever; ipmitool presence is reported as inventory only), supersede AM-6; the lead decides at architecture freeze (DECISIONS D-07).
